newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Govt may buy shares in Russian Svyazinvest units.
newsitem.headline: Govt may buy shares in Russian Svyazinvest units.

text.p: Russia's government may buy up on behalf of national telecoms holding Svyazinvest any extra shares issued by its regional units, and pay for them with state land, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
Valentin Boldin, head of the State Information Committee, told a news conference the government was considering the scheme.
"We're going to open up this path in all sectors of the economy, and we'll start it with the telecoms," he said.

Land on which the regional telecoms sit would be transferred to those companies' balance sheets as payment, but Boldin did not say how the property would be valued. The shares would be bought on behalf on Svyazinvest, he said.
The government wants to help Svyazinvest, which is 100 percent state owned, to maintain control over units. The company does not have cash to buy up any share issues by its units.
Russia is preparing to sell 25 percent plus one share in Svyazinvest. The sale is open to foreign investors and has a starting price of $1.18 billion.
AO Svyazinvest has controlling stakes in 85 regional Russian telecoms and long distance carrier Rostelekom.
